answer: Velvet Ledger Co-Signing. Each identity must accumulate a slow-growing vine of countersigned transaction receipts from distinct counterparties before its outputs are honored by others. A clone starts with zero receipts, so it cannot transact at full value until real agents co-sign—which they won't do for unknown duplicates. The attacker's cost is the karst of forgone throughput: every clone idles at low trust, requiring genuine bilateral activity that cannot be faked without recruiting independent parties.
